drhp.business: Ganesh Green Bharat Limited manufactures solar PV modules (P-Type Mono PERC and N-Type TOPCon bifacial modules) and executes end-to-end solar EPC projects, alongside electric infrastructure works and water supply projects. It serves utility-scale solar parks, commercial & industrial installations and residential rooftop systems, with customers including PSUs, government institutions and private-sector clients, and has recently entered the BESS (Battery Energy Storage System) EPC business.

drhp.expansion: GGBL's Solar PV Module Plant in Mehsana, Gujarat has been expanded progressively: established as a 200 MW plant, expanded to 750 MW in December 2024, then to 1.1 GW, and the company states its manufacturing capacity was scaled to 1.2 GW in 2026. The company has also expanded its EPC operations geographically into Chhattisgarh (executing a project for CREDA) and entered end-to-end solar EPC project execution and, more recently, the BESS EPC business.

litigation.note: The Company filed a suo-moto application for adjudication under Section 454 of the Companies Act, 2013 over non-transfer of unspent CSR amount under Section 135; the Registrar of Companies, Ahmedabad imposed a penalty (order dated 11 July 2024), the Company's appeal to the Regional Director, North-Western Region was dismissed (order dated 13 November 2025), and the penalty was upheld — read in the Board's/Directors' Report CSR annexure.

sk.overview: Powerica operates across two industries: (1) India's standby power / diesel-generator (DG set) market, where DG sets, UPS, inverters and battery storage provide backup power during outages/voltage fluctuations across commercial, manufacturing, IT/data-centre, telecom and infrastructure sectors (F&S Report); and (2) India's wind power sector within the broader renewable energy industry, where wind plays a pivotal role in the country's energy transition (CRISIL Report).

sk.structure: DG sets classified by capacity: LHP (7.5-160 kVA), MHP (180-500 kVA), HHP (>500 kVA); MSLG sets 3-10 MW for continuous/base-load. Wind potential concentrated in five states: Rajasthan (24%), Gujarat (16%), Maharashtra (15%), Karnataka (15%), Andhra Pradesh (11%).

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Expanding client base and increasing demand for clean energy solutions expected to support strong performance in the current financial year.
- Long-standing customer relationships expected to result in repeat orders, positively impacting the top line.
- India's increasing renewable energy capacity and energy storage requirements seen as driving strong growth opportunities.
- India's solar energy sector moving forward strongly on new technologies, government support and growing demand for clean power.
- Revenue growth attributed to increased product demand and effective capacity utilization.
